- **Websites overview** — the customer's most recent sites as cards, with a "View all" to `/dashboard/websites`.
- **Usage summary** — credits remaining, and `averageBuildCredits()` translated into "about N more builds". Read `lib/credits.ts` for what is genuinely available. There is NO reset date and NO monthly allowance; do not imply one.

- **Thumbnails: nothing captures a screenshot** — no field, no headless browser. Do not render a broken image or a fake screenshot. - The current `NewProjectButton` uses `window.prompt()`. Replace that.

5. `app/api/generate/route.ts` IN FULL — you must know its exact SSE event vocabulary.

The builder deliberately sits OUTSIDE the portal shell — it is full-bleed chat + preview, and a 248px nav rail would eat a fifth of the customer's preview. It carries its own back-to-dashboard affordance. Keep it that way, but make it unmistakably the same product: same tokens, same components, same motion.

## THE TARGET LAYOUT

LEFT: AI chat / prompt panel. RIGHT: live website preview occupying most of the screen. Conversation + live website. That is the core Kodely experience.

## 1. CHAT PANEL

Non-image file upload does NOT exist — no multipart, no object storage. If "stop generation" cannot actually abort the server-side run, then either wire it to a real abort or do not offer a button that only hides the UI.

When a change is submitted, the preview must not just sit there while something happens invisibly.

- Preview goes to `k-preview-busy` (a mild blur — the customer must still recognise their own site underneath, or it reads as replaced rather than edited) with a Kodely progress treatment over it.

Note `lib/build-narration.ts` already exists — check whether it is the intended source of this text.

## 3. PREVIEW

Make it feel like a real browser: URL, desktop/tablet/mobile toggle, refresh, open in new tab, zoom, fullscreen. It must stay fully interactive — read `PreviewFrame.tsx:17-26` for why it is a `srcdoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms"` and no `allow-same-origin`, and do not break that. Note the draft preview has NO working forms by design (`app/api/preview/[id]/[[...path]]/route.ts:46-50`) — do not add a "test your form" affordance that cannot work. "Open in new tab" must point at something that genuinely resolves; work out what that is for a draft vs a published site and say so.

## 4. EVERY STATE, DESIGNED

Empty (no site yet) · Building (initial) · Ready · Updating · Success · Error · Publishing · Published. Each gets deliberate UI. `BuildInterrupted.tsx` already handles one of these — understand it before replacing it.

## 5. VERSION HISTORY

Real and already built: checkpoints (`app/api/projects/[id]/builds/route.ts`), restore (`.../restore/route.ts`), and a real line diff (`diff.ts`, `DiffView.tsx`). Surface it properly — version, time, what changed, view / restore / compare.

**Two truths the UI must carry:** snapshots are PRUNED (kept only for the newest 20 per project, and only those older than 30 days are eligible — see `lib/retention.ts:65,74`), so history is bounded and the list must keep filtering on snapshot survival. And restoring does not refund credits or cancel anything. The existing DiffView already states some of this honestly — preserve that honesty, do not smooth it away.

## 6. MOBILE

Carefully designed, not a shrunk desktop. Chat and preview cannot share a phone screen — decide the interaction (tabs? sheet? swap?) and justify it.

HARD RULES:
- `k-focus` on every interactive element, `k-num` on figures, `k-scroll-x` on wide blocks.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (globals.css already neutralises blur for it).
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` with ZERO errors and ZERO warnings. Run both and fix everything.
- Comment like the rest of this codebase: explain WHY, especially where you rejected an approach.

REPORT BACK: what you built, the REAL SSE vocabulary and how faithfully your steps map to it, every control you considered and did NOT build because it would have been fake, your mobile decision and its justification, and anything untested — say untested rather than overstating.

- Credits **never expire**. There is no monthly allowance and **no reset date** — the spend cap is deliberately a *rolling* 30 days precisely so there is no reset day (`lib/credits.ts:258-262`).

**Do not invent any of it.** Your job is to build the best possible billing and usage experience out of what is genuinely there — which is actually quite a lot — and to state plainly where something does not exist. - The credit statement with its existing paging.
- The spend cap.
- When `billingEnabled()` is false, the statement must still render — the current page is deliberate about this (`app/(portal)/dashboard/page.tsx:45-48` explains why) and you must preserve that.

- **Never build something that only pretends to work.**
- No new npm dependencies. Server Components by default.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element. `k-num` on EVERY figure — this page is nothing but figures. `k-scroll-x` on the statement table.

input.prompt:

YOU OWN: everything under `app/(portal)/settings/`, plus any NEW route you need under `app/api/account/`. Do NOT touch other portal pages, `components/ui/**`, `components/app/**`, or existing `app/api/account/**` route files unless you are adding a new one alongside them.

## TASK — a properly sectioned Settings area

Today it is one 58-line page. Split it into real sections with sub-navigation (tabs or a settings sub-nav — your call, justify it). Do not dump everything on one giant page.

### What is REAL today — wire all of it up properly

- **Spend cap** — `app/(portal)/settings/SpendCapForm.tsx`, `app/api/account/spend-cap/route.ts`. Real.
- **Rewards** — `components/rewards/RewardsCard.tsx`, renders nothing when unconfigured. Real, conditionally.
- **Delete account** — real, two-step with a grace period: `app/api/account/deletion/route.ts`, `.../confirm/route.ts`, `app/api/account/_deletion.ts`. **Currently it lives at `/legal/rights`, NOT in Settings.** It belongs in a Danger Zone here. Do not duplicate the logic — surface the existing flow. Decide whether `/legal/rights` keeps its copy (it probably should, for the legal route) and say what you chose.
- **Data export** — real, streamed JSON: `app/api/account/export/route.ts`. Same situation as above.
- **Email** — readable, display only. There is no change-email route; do not build a field that silently does nothing.

### Two things that are NOT built but ARE cheaply real — build them

1. **Editing `User.name`.** The field exists (`prisma/schema.prisma:22`) and is written at signup and in the Google callback, but there is NO edit path. Add a real one: a route under `app/api/account/`, validated, length-capped, and wired to the form. The name is already used across the portal ("Welcome back, <name>"), so this genuinely matters.

2. **Active sessions list + revoke.** The `Session` model (`prisma/schema.prisma:243-253`) is per-user and fully queryable, but nothing lists or revokes them — logout only kills the current one (`lib/auth.ts:50-55`). The audit called this "the cheapest real feature on the list". Build it: list the customer's sessions, mark the current one, allow revoking others and revoking all. Be careful and correct about which session is the current one, and about not letting someone lock themselves out in a confusing way.

**Read the `Session` model and `lib/auth.ts` carefully first.** If the model does not record enough to describe a session usefully to a human (created date, last seen, user agent, IP), then say exactly what it does and does not record and show only what is true — a session row labelled with invented device details would be worse than a bare timestamp. If you add a field to the schema, note that `prisma db push` has NOT been run and flag it clearly in your report.

### What does NOT exist — do not fake any of it

Avatar upload (no field, no storage) · password change/reset (no route writes `passwordHash` after signup) · 2FA · notification preferences (`lib/notifications/templates.ts:20-21` says outright there is no consent record and no unsubscribe mechanism; the four notification kinds are transactional) · login history (`LoginAttempt` stores hashed buckets *deliberately* without identity, so it can never be shown as "your logins") · workspace / members / roles / invitations (there is no workspace concept anywhere — ownership is one FK, `Project.userId`).

For each of these, decide: omit it entirely, or show it with `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` saying plainly what is missing. Security section in particular should not look empty — sessions and account deletion are real and belong there. Justify your choices in the report.

HARD RULES:
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.**
- No new npm dependencies. Server Components by default; `"use client"` only where interaction needs it.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element, `k-num` on figures.
- Any new API route must check auth itself, validate input, and follow the patterns in the existing `app/api/account/` routes exactly (read two of them before writing one).
- Harden params with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` — never `x in OBJ`.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` on your paths with ZERO errors and ZERO warnings.

REPORT BACK: what you built, exactly what `Session` records and what you therefore could and could not show, which unavailable items you omitted vs surfaced and why, any schema change (flagged loudly), and anything untested.

Your three pages are the hardest ones in this redesign, because **all three sit on top of almost nothing**. The whole job is to make each one genuinely useful and completely honest, instead of a mock. Read the honesty rule at the bottom of `docs/design-system.md` before you start.

## PAGE 1 — Support (`/support`)

What exists:
- An **unauthenticated contact form → email**: `app/api/contact/route.ts`, gated on `isMailConfigured()`. Read it in full — you can reuse the endpoint, but check whether it is rate-limited and whether it accepts an authenticated user's identity.
- **Build feedback** thumbs up/down: `app/api/feedback/route.ts` — writes an `Event` only. **There is no reply path.** Anyone who leaves feedback expecting an answer is currently getting nothing back.
- `components/marketing/ContactForm.tsx` — read it, do not edit it.

What does NOT exist: any ticket model, ticket status, or conversation history. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and `prisma/schema.prisma:219-232` says explicitly it is "Never shown to the customer" — do NOT surface it. There is no support AI assistant.

Build the best real support page possible: a proper authenticated contact form (prefilled with their email, and able to reference a specific site of theirs, which genuinely helps), clear expectations about how they get a reply, and honest self-serve help. **Do not build a fake ticket list, fake ticket statuses, or a chat window with no backend.** If `isMailConfigured()` is false, the page must say what to do instead rather than showing a form that silently fails.

The brief asked for a "Kodely AI Assistant" here. Do not fake one. Report what building a real one would actually take.

## PAGE 2 — Domains (`/dashboard/domains`)

The SEO content on the live site even states custom domains are unsupported (`content/seo/ai-website-builder-vs-hiring-a-web-designer.json:29`).

content.text:
Foundation is in and seven agents are building on it. Here's where this landed.

## The design system (done, verified)

`app/globals.css` now carries a **product** token layer additive to the marketing one — surface ramp, neutrals hue-biased toward the brand rather than grey, semantic status kept deliberately off the brand ramp, a radius *step* (control 10 → card 14 → sheet 20), and a motion scale. All exposed through `@theme inline`, so pages write `bg-surface` / `text-ink-2` / `shadow-e2` instead of arbitrary-value brackets — that bracket habit is most of why the old portal drifted out of alignment with itself.

Dark mode moved to **deep navy-indigo** (`#080714`) per your brief, away from the marketing near-black.

Fifteen primitives in [components/ui](components/ui) and the shell in [components/app](components/app) — collapsible sidebar persisted in a **cookie**, not localStorage, so a collapsed rail doesn't render full-width and snap narrow on every page load. Mobile gets a drawer *and* a thumb-reachable bottom bar, not a squeezed sidebar. `/dashboard` and `/settings` moved into an `app/(portal)/` route group; URLs unchanged.

**One typography decision worth flagging:** I kept Geist rather than introducing a display face. The marketing site your customer just came from is set in Geist, and swapping faces at the `/dashboard` boundary breaks the exact continuity your section 1 asks for. The "premium" is bought with the type scale, tracking, tabular numerals and weight discipline instead.

## The part you need to decide on

I ran a full backend audit before designing anything. **Five things in your brief would have been outright lies on screen:**

| Asked for | Reality |
|---|---|
| "Kodely Pro · $XX/month · next billing Aug 24" | **No subscription exists.** One-off credit packs in Stripe `payment` mode. No plan, price, or renewal anywhere. |
| "Reset date: September 1" | **Credits never expire.** The spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen specifically so there's no reset day. |
| Screenshot thumbnails on site cards | **Nothing captures one.** No field, no headless browser, nowhere to store it. |
| "Archived" filter | **No soft-delete column.** The filter could never match anything. |
| Ticket list with statuses | **No ticket model.** `SupportNote` is admin-only and the schema says outright it's never shown to the customer. |

Domains and Integrations have *nothing* behind them — no model, no field, no route. They're still in the sidebar (marked "Soon") with pages that say plainly what's missing and show what you *do* have, rather than a Connect-domain form that goes nowhere.

Two things weren't built but are cheap and genuinely real, so I commissioned both: **editing your name** (the field exists, there's just no edit path) and an **active-sessions list with revoke** (`Session` is per-user and queryable; logout currently kills only the current one).

## Board

New stage at position 7, **Customer Portal & Builder Overhaul**, with the nine workstreams — plus three decision cards in Needs Attention: custom domains, subscription-vs-credits, and the thumbnail question. Those three are yours to call, not mine.

I'll report each agent as it lands, then do the integration pass and full build. One note: the Figma connector in this session isn't authorized, so I can't read or push designs there — you'd need to connect it from an interactive session if you want that.

**Icons tab: 502 assets, 121.6 kB of source.** icon 147 · flag 250 · gradient 30 · divider 12 · pattern 12 · illustration 12 · mark 11 · backdrop 10 · empty-state 8 · mesh 6 · texture 3 · avatar 1. Delivery form: 256 JSX/inline-SVG, 195 emoji text, 51 CSS. Icon categories: ui 51, services 22, media 17, commerce/food 12 each, contact/social 10 each, nature 8, people 5. Flags: 44 exact SVG, 11 simplified SVG, **195 emoji-only** (i.e. 78% of the "flag" count is text that renders as two grey letter boxes on Windows Chrome/Edge).

**Images tab: 0. Videos tab: 0.** Both truthfully empty — no invented rows.

## The provenance gap (the finding you asked for)

**No asset in the catalogue carries provenance.** There is no `source`, `licence`, `author` or `url` field on `Icon`, `Flag`, `GradientPreset`, `SpotPreset` or any other entry type. What exists is a **prose claim in each module's file header**, made once for the whole file. `lib/assets/provenance.ts` transcribes those four claims into data so the page can render a real column, and the page says on **every tab** — in a red notice, not a footnote — that the column is a per-module claim, not a per-asset record.

Two sub-findings worth acting on:

1. **`lib/assets/patterns.ts` is the weak one.** `icons.ts`, `flags.ts` and `illustrations.ts` each carry an explicit PROVENANCE heading stating that nothing was copied from any library. `patterns.ts` never says it — the conclusion has to be inferred from "generated from arithmetic". I record that as `confidence: "inferred"` and it renders amber in both the table and the panel. It's a one-paragraph fix in that file's header.
2. **There is one raster image in the repo with no recorded origin at all**: `public/marketing/bloom-pilates-hero.jpg` (81.4 kB), referenced by `components/marketing/HeroMock.tsx` as "a real reformer-pilates studio photo". It is marketing chrome, not catalogue, and the agent cannot reach it — but nothing anywhere records where it came from or under what licence. The Images tab surfaces it via a live `public/` scan (evidence, not an assertion) and marks its provenance red. Per `docs/research/asset-sources.md` §5 this is exactly the class of thing that needs a record before it's reused.

The module-level representation is adequate *only* because every asset is in-house work today. The moment one third-party SVG lands in any of those four files, the claim silently becomes false for the whole module — that's stated in the code and on the page.

## Deliberate calls, with reasons

- **All 12 asset kinds live under the "Icons" tab.** Gradients under "Icons" reads oddly, but every asset in the catalogue is inline SVG or CSS, and moving backdrops/gradients into "Images" would make an empty tab look populated and hide the point: the agent cannot place a photograph under any prompt. Filter by kind is right there.
- **"Style" = delivery form** (Inline SVG / CSS / Emoji text), not outline-vs-filled. The catalogue has no stylistic variants — one geometry, three stroke weights — so an outline/filled filter would be fiction. Weight is a separate select, because it's a render option that changes what the agent is handed, not what exists.
- **Search is a literal substring match, not `findAssets()`.** The page says so and points at `GET /api/assets?q=` for the agent's own ranked, synonym-expanded search. Conflating "what's in here" with "what would the model pick" would make both answers less trustworthy.
- **No Prisma model.** The catalogue is literals in `.ts` files and provenance is a property of those literals; a table would be a second copy free to drift, needing seeding on every deploy. When Pixabay/Pexels assets start arriving per-build, *those* are per-site records with timestamps and remote ids — a genuinely different table, and the right time to add one.
- **Audit vocabulary tension, flagged rather than papered over.** By `lib/admin-audit.ts`'s own stated rule (record writes, and reads of surfaces exposing *customer* data), this page belongs in the `/admin/flags` bucket where reads are deliberately unrecorded — it shows only our own data. You asked for the event name, so it's in and it's emitted, with a comment explaining the exception (it's the surface someone reads to answer "were we allowed to put this artwork on that customer's site") and naming the correct reversal if a reviewer disagrees: delete the call site and set `emittedBy: null`. `q` is not logged, per the meta rule.

## Untested

**The rendered page has never been loaded in a browser.** Reaching it needs an admin session against the production Postgres in `.env`, and that DB query was blocked — I did not work around it. What *is* verified: `next build` compiles the route as dynamic, and the whole data layer (502 rows, all four facet builders, filtering, every preview branch, the `public/` scan) was executed directly under `jiti` — 0 rows fall back to a placeholder preview and 0 CSS previews come out empty. Layout, spacing and dark-mode rendering are unverified.

One thing the smoke test caught and corrected: I had written that total bytes move with icon weight. They don't — `1.25`, `1.75` and `2.25` are all four characters, so the three weights cost identical bytes. The page now says that explicitly rather than implying a budget difference that doesn't exist.</result>

**Icons tab: 502 assets, 121.6 kB of source.** icon 147 · flag 250 · gradient 30 · divider 12 · pattern 12 · illustration 12 · mark 11 · backdrop 10 · empty-state 8 · mesh 6 · texture 3 · avatar 1. ## The provenance gap (the finding you asked for)

**No asset in the catalogue carries provenance.** There is no `source`, `licence`, `author` or `url` field on `Icon`, `Flag`, `GradientPreset`, `SpotPreset` or any other entry type. What exists is a **prose claim in each module's file header**, made once for the whole file. `lib/assets/provenance.ts` transcribes those four claims into data so the page can render a real column, and the page says on **every tab** — in a red notice, not a footnote — that the column is a per-module claim, not a per-asset record.

Two sub-findings worth acting on:

1. **`lib/assets/patterns.ts` is the weak one.** `icons.ts`, `flags.ts` and `illustrations.ts` each carry an explicit PROVENANCE heading stating that nothing was copied from any library. `patterns.ts` never says it — the conclusion has to be inferred from "generated from arithmetic". The module-level representation is adequate *only* because every asset is in-house work today. The moment one third-party SVG lands in any of those four files, the claim silently becomes false for the whole module — that's stated in the code and on the page.

Weight is a separate select, because it's a render option that changes what the agent is handed, not what exists.

- **No Prisma model.** The catalogue is literals in `.ts` files and provenance is a property of those literals; a table would be a second copy free to drift, needing seeding on every deploy. **The rendered page has never been loaded in a browser.** Reaching it needs an admin session against the production Postgres in `.env`, and that DB query was blocked — I did not work around it. **Admin asset library is done** — `/admin/assets`, three tabs, backed by the *same* `listAssets()` that `find_assets` is served from, so the ids and byte sizes on screen are measured on the exact string the build agent receives rather than a parallel description of it.

Real counts: **Icons 502** (147 icons, 250 flags, 30 gradients, and the rest). **Images 0. Videos 0** — truthfully empty, no invented rows.

But two findings out of it matter more than the page:

## 195 of your 250 flags are emoji text — and I verified it's live, not theoretical

```
flagsWithSvg() → 55 of 250
listAssets()   → exposes all 250 to find_assets
195 entries contain no <svg> anywhere
```

Windows Chrome and Edge have no colour glyph for regional-indicator pairs, so those render as **two grey letter boxes**. The build agent is offered 195 broken flags against 55 real ones — and `flag:ad` (Andorra), the very first entry in the catalogue, is one of the broken ones.

This hits exactly where it hurts: the agent reaches for flags on language switchers, shipping lists, "we serve these countries" strips. A customer's restaurant site shows a row of `▯▯ ▯▯ ▯▯` and they'll have no idea why. Carded HIGH — the fix is to drop the emoji entries (250 → 55, honest), draw more SVGs, or make `find_assets` refuse to return one. Not to keep the count at 250.

## One photo on your live marketing site has no recorded licence

`public/marketing/bloom-pilates-hero.jpg`, used by `HeroMock.tsx`, described in that file as "a real reformer-pilates studio photo". Every other visual in the product is in-house generated work with a provenance claim in its module header. This one is a photograph, and photographs have owners. Nothing anywhere records where it came from.

The structural version of that problem is also carded: **provenance is a per-module prose claim, not a per-asset field.** That holds only while everything is in-house. The licence audit recommends vendoring upstream OSS icon packs — the moment one third-party SVG lands in `icons.ts`, that module's claim becomes silently false for all 147 icons in it. So per-entry provenance fields need to go in *before* the first vendored pack, not after.

Six shapes reach the client: `text` (prose deltas), `progress`, `status`, `file{path,action}`, `done{credits,remaining,filesWritten,buildId,repairAttempts,repairWaived,waivedCredits}`, `error{message}`. **`usage` is produced by the agent but consumed server-side for billing and never forwarded** — the client cannot see spend while a build runs.

The two text channels have enumerable producers:
- `progress` ← `narrateTool()`: `Writing …` / `Writing a file`, `Updating …` / `Making an edit`, `Removing …` / `Removing a file`, `Looking through the project`, `Running a command`; plus `Picking out icons and artwork` (agent.ts:411) and `Compiling the site` (route:305, direct send, bypasses the dedupe).
- `status` ← only two: `Building your site…` / `Applying your changes…` (SDK engine, once) and `Build didn't compile — fixing it…` (route, per repair).

**The six requested steps are not supportable.** The stream carries no planning marker, no designing marker, and cannot separate layout work from copy work — a write to `Hero.tsx` is one `file` event either way. | Step | Completed by |
|---|---|
| Creating your project | `POST /api/projects` returns an id |
| Sending your brief to Kodely | `POST /api/generate` answers 200 with a body — i.e. kill switch, balance, spend cap and rate limit all passed and a Build row exists |
| Reading the brief and the starter files | first write evidence: a `file` event, or a `progress` line matching `/^(Writing\|Updating\|Removing\|Making an edit)\b/` |
| Writing your site's files | `progress === "Compiling the site"` |
| Compiling the site | `done` |

content.text:
Three more landed. Highlights, then what I fixed myself.

## Home + My Websites

The **thumbnail** call: a generated cover, deliberately *not* shaped like a screenshot — no browser chrome, no fake page layout. If the project has a brand kit it uses the site's **real** `palette.primary → secondary`; otherwise a deterministic hash of the slug into curated pairs, so it's stable forever and distinct between neighbours. Labelled on the page in plain words: *"Covers are generated from each site's own colours — Kodely doesn't capture screenshots."*

The **Building** filter shipped with a stated rule rather than being dropped: a site reads as Building only while a `RUNNING` build is **younger than 10 minutes** — double the `maxDuration = 300` the generate route itself enforces — so an abandoned SSE row collapses instead of claiming to build forever. **Archive** stays visible in the menu with "Doesn't exist yet", because people go looking for it.

It also caught that **Publish 400s when there's no compiled draft tree**, and now greys the action with "Nothing built yet" rather than letting it fail.

## Usage + Billing

Everything on your billing list got refused and replaced with something true: no plan, no price, no renewal, no saved card, no invoices, no reset date. In their place, a **pack comparison built from the real `CREDIT_PACKS`** — credits, price, price per credit, and "about N builds" computed from *that customer's own measured average*, showing `—` until they have a charged build rather than dividing by a global constant.

Two things I didn't ask for and am glad it built:

- **A "Websites you've deleted" reconciliation row.** Deleting a project cascades its builds and SET NULLs `buildId`, so those charges genuinely can't be attributed. Rather than let the per-site numbers quietly fail to sum to the ledger total, it shows the gap and names it.
- **"What you weren't charged for"** — failed builds, repaired builds, and credits absorbed on repairs. It rounds *down* on purpose, since `creditsCharged` is ceil-rounded, so it understates what you absorbed. That's the only safe direction on a page a customer reads.

And a refusal I didn't think to ask for: **`Build.costMicros` is never rendered as money anywhere.** That's your model spend and the cost side of your margins — it's used inside arithmetic and nothing else. Every figure on both pages is in credits.

## Create Website

It refused the six-step progress list and shipped **five**, each with exactly one observable trigger, in a reducer with **no clock access** so it physically cannot self-advance. Your requested "Planning the structure" and "Designing the layout" have no marker in the stream at all — a write to `Hero.tsx` is one `file` event whether it's layout or copy.

Two real findings out of it:

**Navigating mid-build kills the build.** Closing the response body fires `cancel()` and aborts server-side. It now aborts on unmount deliberately, so "leaving stops the build" is *true* rather than hopeful, and says so next to a real Stop button.

**A build can finish and take you below zero.** The balance is checked when a build *starts*, never again at settle — `chargeForBuild` just writes `balance - credits`. 300 credits, a build that lands at 480, you end at −180. ### New API routes (both auth-check themselves, validate, and mirror the existing `app/api/account/` shape)

- `app/api/account/profile/route.ts` — `GET` + `PUT { name }`. Validation lives in `app/api/account/_profile.ts` (shared with the form so client and server agree on the cap): 80 code points max, whitespace collapsed, control characters / zero-width / **bidi-override characters stripped** (the name renders inline in "Welcome back, ‹name›", and an unterminated RLO reverses the rest of the line — React escapes markup, not text direction). `""` and `null` both clear it. Body parsed with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`, never `in`.
- `app/api/account/sessions/route.ts` — `GET` list, `DELETE` with three shapes: `{id}` (one other session), `{scope:"others"}`, `{scope:"all"}`. `{id}` equal to the caller's own session is refused with a 409 that names the alternative rather than silently signing them out. `"all"` deletes every row *and* clears the cookie via `destroySession()` (the deletion/confirm route's pattern), returns `signedOut: true`, and the client `router.replace("/login")`s. Every `WHERE` repeats the session's own `userId`, so another account's session id is indistinguishable from one that doesn't exist. Sending both `id` and `scope`, or neither, is a 400.

## What `Session` actually records — and what I therefore could not show

```
id · userId · tokenHash (SHA-256) · expiresAt · createdAt
```

That's the whole row, and `lib/auth.ts` writes nothing else. **No user agent, no IP, no last-seen, no device, no location, and nothing joins to it.** So each row shows exactly three true things: when the sign-in happened, when it expires, and whether it's this browser. The card says so out loud — that Kodely doesn't store the browser/device/IP and *will not guess* — so nobody reads two dates as a truncated version of something richer.

**I did not add schema fields, deliberately** (so: no schema change, nothing to `prisma db push`):
- A UA/IP column is *new personal data*, and both `/legal/rights` and `app/api/account/export/route.ts` enumerate in writing everything the database holds — the export explicitly lists IP addresses under what is *not* included. Adding the column silently makes two published documents wrong.

content.thinking:
The lint issue is the synchronous state resets at the top of the effect that fire when the reload nonce changes. I'm thinking the cleanest fix is moving those resets so they only happen asynchronously inside the fetch logic, since the lint rule specifically targets synchronous setState calls in the effect body, not async ones.

Actually, a better approach is consolidating loading, doc, and error into one state object keyed by nonce, deriving loading as whether the stored nonce matches the current one — this eliminates the resets entirely and removes two state variables. I'm considering how this affects the reload UX, since clearing the doc during reload versus keeping the stale doc visible are both reasonable options, and I want to keep the derived rendering logic simple.

I derive `loading` by comparing the nonce the effect last answered against the one it was asked, avoiding an extra reset and re-render. On error I clear the doc and let the error branch render, and the `finally { setLoading(false) }` block disappears entirely. Aborted effects simply skip setting result, so stale nonces are handled correctly since a nonce change triggers a fresh effect anyway.

I'll keep `key={nonce}` on the iframe so it remounts on nonce change, then apply the edit.

# Kodely product design system

The contract for the customer-facing portal (`app/(portal)/**`) and the builder
(`app/projects/[id]/**`). Marketing pages (`app/page.tsx`, `/pricing`, `/blog`,
`/templates`, `/wizard`) are a **separate** system — do not repoint their tokens.

## The one-sentence brief

An AI website builder that happens to have a customer portal around it — not a
dashboard that happens to contain a builder. The primary action is always
"build something".

---

## Tokens

Defined in `app/globals.css`, exposed to Tailwind via `@theme inline`. **Use the
Tailwind class, never a raw hex and never an arbitrary-value bracket.**

### Surface

| Class | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `bg-canvas` | The page behind panels. Set by `AppShell`; pages never set it. |
| `bg-surface` | Cards, panels, the sidebar. |
| `bg-surface-2` | Hover, inset rows, quiet fills. |
| `bg-surface-3` | Track of a progress bar, the deepest step. |
| `bg-inset` | Code/preview wells. |

### Line

`border-hair` (default for cards) · `border-line-mid` (inputs, menus) ·
`border-line-strong` (emphasis, pending step outline)

### Text

`text-ink` (primary) · `text-ink-2` (secondary/body) · `text-ink-3` (tertiary,
placeholder, disabled) · `text-ink-inv` (on a brand fill)

### Brand

`text-brand` `bg-brand` `bg-brand-tint` `bg-brand-tint-2` `text-brand-ink`

`--brand-gradient` is a **fill of last resort**. Exactly one element per view may
carry it: the primary button. Do not gradient headings, cards, borders or icons.

### Status

`ok` `warn` `danger` `info`, each with a `-tint` companion
(`text-ok` / `bg-ok-tint`). Status colour is never the brand colour.

### Radius / elevation / motion

`rounded-sm|md|lg|xl|2xl` (8/10/14/20/28px) · `shadow-e1|e2|e3` ·
`duration-[var(--t-1)]` 120ms, `--t-2` 200ms, `--t-3` 380ms ·
`ease-[var(--ease)]`

---

## Utility classes

`k-focus` — **put this on every interactive element.** One focus ring, product-wide.
`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.

---

## Components (`components/ui/`)

Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**

| Component | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
| `Spinner` | |

## Shell (`components/app/`)

`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
`ToastProvider`.

Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.

---

## AI progress is one object, not three spinners

`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.

**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
and not a progress bar.

---

## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)

| Thing | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
| **Support tickets** | No ticket model. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and explicitly never shown to the customer. |
| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |

**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, ARE cheaply real** — the
`Session` model is per-user and queryable.

### The rule

A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.

READ FIRST:

WHAT I ALREADY FIXED (do not redo, but do sanity-check):

- `preview/StandalonePreview.tsx` had a synchronous `setState` at the top of its effect. I replaced the separate doc/error/loading state with one `{nonce, doc, error}` object and derived `loading` from a nonce comparison.

YOU OWN: everything under `app/projects/[id]/`. Do NOT touch `app/(portal)/**`, `components/ui/**`, `components/app/**`, or `lib/**`. If a shared primitive needs a change, report it instead.

## VERIFY AGAINST THE ORIGINAL BRIEF — and finish whatever is missing

For each item below, determine whether it is genuinely done, half-done, or absent, then finish it. Be honest in your report about which it was when you arrived.

1. **Layout** — left chat panel, right live preview taking most of the screen.
2. **Chat panel as an assistant** — named header, real status badge, history, bottom-pinned input, context-dependent suggested follow-ups. Controls only where real: regenerate, undo, retry, stop generation, image attach. **Non-image upload does not exist** — no multipart, no object storage. 3. **AI progress driven by REAL SSE signals.** The predecessor built `build-steps.ts` as a reducer. content.text:
**Recovered.** The builder agent's damage was one missing prop — it died on the exact line it said it was on. I finished that wire myself and fixed one other thing it left.

The missing piece was the honest error copy, and it needed three branches, not one, because the failures are genuinely different:

- **Retry offered** — the route refused before writing anything (kill switch, balance, spend cap, rate limit). No `Build` row, no `Message` row. A retry really is a clean re-run.
- **No retry, files written** — the build started and died partway. *"Kodely had already changed some files before this stopped, so your site is part-way through the edit. You weren't charged. Check the preview, then either describe what to fix, or undo this build from History."*
- **No retry, nothing written** — nothing changed, send it again.

The reason there's no "Try again" on the second two is real: `/api/generate` writes the user's `Message` row *before* running, so resending would be classified as an **edit** against a half-built site rather than a re-run.

I also fixed `StandalonePreview` — it reset three state variables synchronously at the top of its effect on every Reload. Replaced with one `{nonce, doc, error}` object and `loading` derived from a nonce comparison, so there's no reset and no second render pass.

## Everything green

```
tsc --noEmit          clean
eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0   clean
303 tests             303 pass
npm run build         compiled
```

## Settings

Four routed sections, and the two new features are genuinely real. The name validator strips **bidi-override characters** — that's a proper catch: the name renders inline in "Welcome back, ‹name›", and an unterminated RLO reverses the rest of the line. React escapes markup, not text direction. I've carded a sweep of every other free-text field for the same hole.

The sessions screen is deliberately spare, and the reasoning is the best thing in that report. `Session` records only `id · userId · tokenHash · expiresAt · createdAt` — no device, no IP, no last-seen. The obvious "improvement" is a user-agent column, and it declined: **both `/legal/rights` and the data export enumerate in writing everything the database holds, and the export explicitly lists IP addresses under what is *not* collected.** Adding that column silently makes two published documents false. Carded so the next person doesn't walk into it.

It also caught that its own change had falsified a sentence on the legal rights page ("There is no self-serve editor for your name…") and fixed it rather than leaving it.

I repointed seven deep links that expected the spend cap and were landing on the wrong tab.

Board's at 52 in Done. Builder verification and a cross-page consistency pass are running now — the consistency pass is the one thing no individual agent could do, since none of them could see each other's work.

CONTEXT: Kodely is an AI website builder. Published sites currently live only at `<slug>.kodely.site`, served from Postgres rows by `app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts` and routed by `proxy.ts`. There is NO custom-domain support of any kind: no Domain model, no DNS code, no certificate handling. The owner wants a **direct integration with Nxeon** — their own hosting product — so a customer can keep the free Kodely subdomain OR get the site hosted on a real server with a custom domain.

READ FIRST:
- `app/api/projects/[id]/publish/route.ts` — how publishing works today, and the `KODELY_SITES_BASE` env var.
- `app/api/site/[slug]/site-host.ts` — the host allowlist. **Read lines 68-76 carefully: this is a SECURITY CONTROL, not config.** It is what stops customer A's markup being served from customer B's origin, where `'self'` and `frame-ancestors 'self'` resolve to the victim.
- `app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts` — how a published site is served, including CSP.
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — the `Project` model and how `slug` works.
- `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:49-73` — why a slug is never regenerated.
- `lib/site-seo.ts:29-53` — how the public URL is derived.
- `docs/design-system.md` — the honesty rules.

## DELIVERABLE 1 — Deep research (`docs/research/nxeon-hosting.md`)

Research thoroughly, using the web, how to architect a website-builder → hosting-provider integration. Cover at minimum:

1. **Domain registration and purchase** — what a reseller/API integration actually involves (registrar APIs, EPP, ICANN requirements, WHOIS/RDAP privacy, transfer locks, renewal and expiry handling, TLD-specific rules). Who is the registrant of record, and what does that mean if a customer leaves?
2. **Domain verification** — proving the customer controls a domain they already own. DNS TXT vs CNAME vs HTTP file. Why verification is a security boundary and not a formality (hostnames are globally unique and adversarial).
3. **DNS** — what records need to exist, apex vs www (the CNAME-at-apex problem, ALIAS/ANAME/flattening), TTL strategy during cutover, and how to detect propagation honestly rather than guessing.
4. **TLS certificates** — ACME/Let's Encrypt issuance and *unattended renewal* per customer domain, HTTP-01 vs DNS-01 vs TLS-ALPN-01 and which fits, rate limits and how to avoid hitting them, key storage, and what breaks silently at 90 days.
5. **Provisioning and deployment** — how a site's files get from Kodely's Postgres onto a real server, atomic deploys/rollback, cache invalidation, and what happens on republish.
6. **Billing hand-off** — the customer is paying Kodely; hosting costs money. Who bills whom, and how do you handle a lapsed payment without silently taking someone's site offline.
7. **Failure modes and the honest UI states** they imply: pending verification, DNS not propagated, cert issuance failed, provisioning failed, domain expiring, payment lapsed.
8. **What the competition does** — how Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, Vercel, Netlify, Framer and Lovable handle custom domains and what their flows look like. Note specifically what makes a flow feel simple to a non-technical customer.

Cite sources. Where you cannot verify something, write UNSURE — do not guess.

## DELIVERABLE 2 — The Kodely-side design

Write this into the same doc, then implement the parts that do not need the Nxeon API:

- **`Domain` Prisma model** — propose it in the doc with full reasoning (fields, states, indexes, uniqueness constraints, what cascades on project deletion, and why). **Do NOT edit `prisma/schema.prisma`** — the schema has uncommitted changes and `prisma db push` has not been run. Put the proposed model in the doc as a code block and flag it clearly.
- **`lib/nxeon/` — a typed client behind an interface.** Define the full surface Kodely needs (`purchaseDomain`, `verifyDomain`, `provisionSite`, `deploySite`, `certificateStatus`, `removeSite`, whatever else research says is needed), as TypeScript interfaces with real types and thorough doc comments. Ship a single implementation that **throws a clear "not configured" error**, gated on an env var named after the SERVICE (follow the precedent in `app/api/import/fetcher.ts` — read it and match the naming reasoning). This must be genuinely wired so that swapping in a real client is a one-file change.
- **A state machine for a domain's lifecycle**, as real TypeScript with exhaustive states, plus the honest customer-facing sentence for each state.
- **What must change in `siteHostAllowed()`** and the exact invariant that must be preserved. Be explicit and careful — write it as a spec, do not change the function.

## HARD RULES
- Do NOT edit `prisma/schema.prisma`, `app/api/site/**`, `proxy.ts`, or anything under `app/(portal)/**` — other agents are working there.
- No new npm dependencies.
- Everything you ship must compile: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0`, zero errors and zero warnings.
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.** A stub that throws "not configured" is honest. A stub that returns fake success is not.

REPORT BACK: the shape of the integration, the five hardest problems and your recommended approach to each, what you implemented vs specified, and a clear list of exactly what you need from the Nxeon API to finish — that list is what I will hand the owner.

- `prisma/schema.prisma` — the `Project` model and how `slug` works.
- `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:49-73` — why a slug is never regenerated.
- `lib/site-seo.ts:29-53` — how the public URL is derived.
- `docs/design-system.md` — the honesty rules.

## DELIVERABLE 1 — Deep research (`docs/research/nxeon-hosting.md`)

Research thoroughly, using the web, how to architect a website-builder → hosting-provider integration. Cover at minimum:

1. **Domain registration and purchase** — what a reseller/API integration actually involves (registrar APIs, EPP, ICANN requirements, WHOIS/RDAP privacy, transfer locks, renewal and expiry handling, TLD-specific rules). Who is the registrant of record, and what does that mean if a customer leaves?
2. **Domain verification** — proving the customer controls a domain they already own. DNS TXT vs CNAME vs HTTP file. Why verification is a security boundary and not a formality (hostnames are globally unique and adversarial).
3. **DNS** — what records need to exist, apex vs www (the CNAME-at-apex problem, ALIAS/ANAME/flattening), TTL strategy during cutover, and how to detect propagation honestly rather than guessing.
4. **TLS certificates** — ACME/Let's Encrypt issuance and *unattended renewal* per customer domain, HTTP-01 vs DNS-01 vs TLS-ALPN-01 and which fits, rate limits and how to avoid hitting them, key storage, and what breaks silently at 90 days.
5. **Provisioning and deployment** — how a site's files get from Kodely's Postgres onto a real server, atomic deploys/rollback, cache invalidation, and what happens on republish.
6. **Billing hand-off** — the customer is paying Kodely; hosting costs money. Who bills whom, and how do you handle a lapsed payment without silently taking someone's site offline.
7. **Failure modes and the honest UI states** they imply: pending verification, DNS not propagated, cert issuance failed, provisioning failed, domain expiring, payment lapsed.
8. **What the competition does** — how Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, Vercel, Netlify, Framer and Lovable handle custom domains and what their flows look like. Note specifically what makes a flow feel simple to a non-technical customer.

Cite sources. Where you cannot verify something, write UNSURE — do not guess.

## DELIVERABLE 2 — The Kodely-side design

Write this into the same doc, then implement the parts that do not need the Nxeon API:

- **`Domain` Prisma model** — propose it in the doc with full reasoning (fields, states, indexes, uniqueness constraints, what cascades on project deletion, and why). **Do NOT edit `prisma/schema.prisma`** — the schema has uncommitted changes and `prisma db push` has not been run. Put the proposed model in the doc as a code block and flag it clearly.
- **`lib/nxeon/` — a typed client behind an interface.** Define the full surface Kodely needs (`purchaseDomain`, `verifyDomain`, `provisionSite`, `deploySite`, `certificateStatus`, `removeSite`, whatever else research says is needed), as TypeScript interfaces with real types and thorough doc comments. Ship a single implementation that **throws a clear "not configured" error**, gated on an env var named after the SERVICE (follow the precedent in `app/api/import/fetcher.ts` — read it and match the naming reasoning). This must be genuinely wired so that swapping in a real client is a one-file change.
- **A state machine for a domain's lifecycle**, as real TypeScript with exhaustive states, plus the honest customer-facing sentence for each state.
- **What must change in `siteHostAllowed()`** and the exact invariant that must be preserved. Be explicit and careful — write it as a spec, do not change the function.

## HARD RULES
- Do NOT edit `prisma/schema.prisma`, `app/api/site/**`, `proxy.ts`, or anything under `app/(portal)/**` — other agents are working there.
- No new npm dependencies.
- Everything you ship must compile: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0`, zero errors and zero warnings.
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.** A stub that throws "not configured" is honest. A stub that returns fake success is not.

REPORT BACK: the shape of the integration, the five hardest problems and your recommended approach to each, what you implemented vs specified, and a clear list of exactly what you need from the Nxeon API to finish — that list is what I will hand the owner.

input.prompt:
You are working in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16.3.1, React 19, Tailwind v4, Prisma 6 + Postgres, TypeScript strict; lucide-react available; NO new dependencies).

TASK: Build a **real support ticketing system** — customer-facing tickets that land in the admin portal, with replies the customer can read in-app.

READ FIRST:
1. `docs/design-system.md` — the binding contract, tokens, primitives, honesty rules.
2. `components/ui/*` — the primitives. Import them; never hand-roll a second version.
3. `app/(portal)/support/page.tsx` + `ContactPanel.tsx` — what exists today (an authenticated contact form → email). **Another agent may be making small consistency edits here concurrently** — re-read before you write.
4. `prisma/schema.prisma` — especially `SupportNote` (admin-only, `prisma/schema.prisma:219-232`, "Never shown to the customer"), `FormSubmission` (a good precedent for a customer-generated record with read state), `Event`, `AdminAuditLog`.
5. `app/admin/feedback/**` — the existing admin surface for customer signal, its actions file, and its visual language. Your admin page must match it, not the customer design system.
6. `lib/admin-audit.ts` — the audit vocabulary is CLOSED. Add your event names to it.
7. `lib/mail.ts` and `lib/notifications/**` — how email is sent and gated on `isMailConfigured()`.

## WHAT TO BUILD

**Schema.** Propose and add the models — a ticket and its messages, with status, subject, the customer's project reference where relevant, timestamps, and read state on BOTH sides (the customer needs to know staff replied; staff need to know what is unanswered). Think carefully about:
- Status vocabulary. Keep it small and meaningful. Every status must be one a human actually sets or the system can derive.
- Who authored a message — customer vs staff — and that a staff reply is visible while `SupportNote` remains invisible. **Do not conflate the two.** `SupportNote` is an internal note and must stay that way; explain in a comment how they differ.
- What happens on account deletion. Read `app/api/account/_deletion.ts` and make your models consistent with it, and update the deletion preview counts if they enumerate tables.
- Whether tickets belong in the data export (`app/api/account/export/route.ts` enumerates everything the DB holds about a person — if you add a table holding their words, that document becomes incomplete unless you add it).

**IMPORTANT:** `prisma db push` has NOT been run on this working copy and there are uncommitted schema changes. Add your models to `prisma/schema.prisma`, run `npx prisma generate` so types exist, and **flag loudly in your report that a `db push` is required**. Do not attempt to push.

**Customer side (`/support`).** Keep everything honest that the current page does well — read it first, it is careful. Add: create a ticket (subject, body, optional site reference), a list of the customer's tickets with real status, a thread view where they can read staff replies and reply back. If `isMailConfigured()` is false, tickets must still work in-app — the email is a notification, not the mechanism. Say so.

**Also required on `/support`: a Kodely gradient card showing their credits.** Use `--brand-gradient`. This is the one place per page the gradient may be used as a fill. Show balance and something genuinely useful next to it (e.g. about how many builds that is, from `averageBuildCredits()`); do NOT show a plan, a monthly allowance or a reset date — none of those exist.

**Admin side (`/admin/support` or extend `/admin/feedback`).** Your call, justified: list, filter by status, open a thread, reply, change status. Must call `getAdminUser()` itself (the layout is not the sole boundary — see `app/admin/layout.tsx`). Add a nav entry. Harden params with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`, never `x in OBJ`.

**Notifications.** When staff reply, the customer should find out. Read `lib/notifications/**` for the existing transactional-email pattern and follow it exactly, including its gating. Note the codebase states plainly there is no consent record and no unsubscribe mechanism — a reply notification is transactional, so it fits, but say why in a comment.

## HARD RULES
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.** No fake agents, no fake avatars, no invented SLA, no "typically replies within a few hours" unless something measures it.
- Rate-limit ticket creation. Note that `/api/contact`'s existing limiter is per-IP and in-process — do not copy that flaw for an authenticated endpoint; key on the user.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element, `k-num` on figures, `k-scroll-x` on wide tables.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0`, and `node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` (303 currently pass). Run all three.
- Do NOT touch `app/projects/[id]/**`, `components/ui/**`, `components/app/**`, or other `app/(portal)/dashboard/**` pages.

REPORT BACK: the schema you added (and the loud db-push flag), your status vocabulary and why, how you kept `SupportNote` distinct, what happens on account deletion and export, and anything untested.

input.prompt:
You are working in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16.3.1, React 19, Tailwind v4, TypeScript strict; framer-motion + lucide-react available; NO new dependencies).

TASK: Build the **inline 5-stage build wizard**, as a self-contained component another agent will mount on the Create Website page. Today "Help me write it" navigates away to `/wizard`; it must instead open in place.

READ FIRST:
1. `docs/design-system.md` — binding contract.
2. `components/ui/*` — `Modal`, `Field`, `Segmented`, `Badge`, `Button`, `Card`, `AIProgress`. Import them; never hand-roll a second version.
3. `components/wizard/PromptWizard.tsx` (695 lines), `LookPicker.tsx`, `ImportStep.tsx`, and `lib/wizard.ts` — **the existing wizard and its prompt-assembly logic. This is your foundation. Read all of it.** The public `/wizard` page must keep working unchanged.
4. `lib/brand-kit.ts` — colour/brand vocabulary.
5. `lib/templates.ts` — how a good build brief actually reads. The 23 prompts are the quality bar for what your wizard must assemble.
6. `lib/agent.ts` — the SYSTEM prompt. **Read what a generated site actually IS**: one page, no backend, no accounts, no database. This governs which "features" are honestly offerable.
7. `app/api/import/fetcher.ts` — the URL-import gate, and why it is named after the service.

## YOU OWN
`components/wizard/InlineWizard.tsx` (new) and any new files under `components/wizard/`, plus `lib/features.ts` (new). Do NOT edit `PromptWizard.tsx`, `LookPicker.tsx`, `ImportStep.tsx`, `lib/wizard.ts`, `app/wizard/**`, `app/**`, `components/ui/**`, or `components/templates/**` (another agent owns that).

If you need logic out of `PromptWizard.tsx` or `lib/wizard.ts`, **import it if it is exported; copy it into your own file if it is not.** Do not edit theirs.

## THE EXACT INTERFACE — another agent mounts this

```tsx
export type InlineWizardResult = {
  /** The finished, editable build prompt. */
  prompt: string;
  logoDataUrl?: string;
  palette?: string[];
};

export function InlineWizard(props: {
  open: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  onComplete: (result: InlineWizardResult) => void;
}): React.ReactNode;
```

A stub with this exact signature already exists at that path. Replace it.

## THE FIVE STAGES

1. **Describe** — what are you building, in their own words.
2. **Site details** — name, location, what they do, contact details, hours; whatever the brief genuinely needs.
3. **Style & layout** — colour scheme, mood, typography feel, layout shape. Logo upload here.
4. **Features** — see below.
5. **Review & build** — the assembled prompt, fully editable, with an honest credit estimate (`estimateCredits("create")`, shown as a RANGE not a quote).

Clean and organised, with the **Kodely logo above the wizard** (`components/marketing/Logo.tsx` exports `Logo` and `Mark`). A clear stage indicator. Back and forward without losing answers. Every stage skippable — someone must be able to reach Review from stage 1.

## STAGE 4 AND `lib/features.ts` — THE PART THAT NEEDS JUDGEMENT

Build a **feature library**: a typed catalogue of site features a customer can toggle on, where each feature contributes a precise, well-written fragment to the build prompt. This is foundation work — it should be easy to add features later.

**The hard constraint, and you must respect it:** read `lib/agent.ts` and find out exactly what a generated site can and cannot do. It is a single-page React app with no backend, no database and no accounts. `lib/site-forms.ts` means contact forms on PUBLISHED sites genuinely work and email the owner — verify that yourself and note that draft previews do not have working forms.

So: a booking system with real availability, user logins, e-commerce checkout, and a searchable database are **not honestly offerable**. A contact form, an opening-hours table, a gallery, a pricing table, testimonials, an FAQ accordion, a map embed (check the CSP first — `app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts` sets `connect-src 'none'` and a restrictive `img-src`; a third-party map iframe will very likely be blocked, so **verify before offering it**) probably are.

**Categorise every feature you consider as offerable or not, and put the not-offerable ones in your report with the reason.** Do not silently drop them and do not offer them greyed-out with a fake "Pro" lock. If a feature is nearly-offerable, say what would make it real.

Each feature needs: id, label, a one-line customer-facing description that is TRUE, a category, and the prompt fragment. Where a feature has a caveat the customer should know (e.g. "the form works once your site is published, not in preview"), the UI must say it.

## HARD RULES
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.** This applies doubly to the feature list — every toggle is a promise about the finished site.
- Logo upload: follow `app/(portal)/dashboard/new/image.ts` (read it) so output always matches the `data:image/(png|jpeg|webp);base64,` regex the generate route enforces.
- `k-focus` everywhere, works in both themes, focus moves sensibly on stage change, and the stage indicator is announced to assistive tech.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components --max-warnings=0`, zero errors zero warnings.

REPORT BACK: your feature library and — importantly — the full list of features you REFUSED to offer with the reason for each, what you reused vs copied from the existing wizard, your verdict on map embeds under the real CSP, and anything untested.

Seven agents running now. Here's the state and one thing I need from you.

## Two of your asks are already true

**30-day login persistence exists** — `SESSION_DAYS = 30` with a matching cookie expiry. The real gap is that `MarketingNav` never checks for a session, so it always says "Sign in / Get started". I've had that agent verify one thing worth knowing: whether it's a *hard* 30 days from sign-in or a *sliding* 30 days from last use. Those are meaningfully different promises and you should know which one you're making.

**The homepage prompt box already has voice-to-text** — Web Speech API with a mic button. Porting it to the Create page gives you that for free rather than rebuilding it.

## Sidebar — done

Restyled to the Kodely theme: softer 14px radii on nav rows, a bordered disc for the collapse control (a bare glyph in a panel corner reads as decoration and people didn't find it), and a thicker active rail marker.

At the bottom, the **brand-gradient credits card** from your mockup, plus the theme toggle and a "Bug or idea" menu linking to `/support?topic=bug` and `?topic=feature`. Same footer appears in the mobile drawer, so both widths have those three things in the same place.

One deliberate deviation from your mockup: **no progress bar and no "750 / 1,000" on that card.** There's no allowance for it to be a fraction of — credits are bought in packs and never expire — so a bar would have to invent a denominator. It shows the balance and "about N more builds" instead, which is what people actually plan in.

## What's building

| | |
|---|---|
| **Nxeon** | Deep research + integration spec, `Domain` state machine, typed client behind an interface that throws "not configured" until wired |
| **Support** | Real ticketing — schema, customer threads, staff replies, admin portal, gradient credits card |
| **Templates** | Modal gallery with generated covers per template, then a per-template intake stage (the questions each of the 23 actually needs) |
| **Wizard** | Inline 5-stage, plus `lib/features.ts` — a feature library where every toggle is a promise the built site can keep |
| **Marketing nav** | Signed-in detection without quietly making your whole SEO site dynamic |
| **Builder + consistency** | Still finishing from the earlier wave |

Usage/Billing/Domains restyle, the Create page prompt-box port, and thumbnails are queued behind the consistency agent — it currently owns those files and I'd rather not have two agents writing the same page.

**Billing:** going with credit packs, matching your mockup's structure. Most of it maps cleanly onto real data — the stat row, the credits-over-time chart, "where your credits went" per site, the spending cap, and the "what isn't charged" strip all work as drawn. The plan card, invoices, saved cards and the storage/bandwidth bars get replaced with true equivalents.

**What I need from you:** the Nxeon repo path or API docs. The agent is designing against an interface right now, so pointing me at it turns the stub into a real integration in one file.

# Kodely product design system

The contract for the customer-facing portal (`app/(portal)/**`) and the builder
(`app/projects/[id]/**`). Marketing pages (`app/page.tsx`, `/pricing`, `/blog`,
`/templates`, `/wizard`) are a **separate** system — do not repoint their tokens.

## The one-sentence brief

An AI website builder that happens to have a customer portal around it — not a
dashboard that happens to contain a builder. The primary action is always
"build something".

---

## Tokens

Defined in `app/globals.css`, exposed to Tailwind via `@theme inline`. **Use the
Tailwind class, never a raw hex and never an arbitrary-value bracket.**

### Surface

| Class | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `bg-canvas` | The page behind panels. Set by `AppShell`; pages never set it. |
| `bg-surface` | Cards, panels, the sidebar. |
| `bg-surface-2` | Hover, inset rows, quiet fills. |
| `bg-surface-3` | Track of a progress bar, the deepest step. |
| `bg-inset` | Code/preview wells. |

### Line

`border-hair` (default for cards) · `border-line-mid` (inputs, menus) ·
`border-line-strong` (emphasis, pending step outline)

### Text

`text-ink` (primary) · `text-ink-2` (secondary/body) · `text-ink-3` (tertiary,
placeholder, disabled) · `text-ink-inv` (on a brand fill)

### Brand

`text-brand` `bg-brand` `bg-brand-tint` `bg-brand-tint-2` `text-brand-ink`

`--brand-gradient` is a **fill of last resort**. Exactly one element per view may
carry it: the primary button. Do not gradient headings, cards, borders or icons.

### Status

`ok` `warn` `danger` `info`, each with a `-tint` companion
(`text-ok` / `bg-ok-tint`). Status colour is never the brand colour.

### Radius / elevation / motion

`rounded-sm|md|lg|xl|2xl` (8/10/14/20/28px) · `shadow-e1|e2|e3` ·
`duration-[var(--t-1)]` 120ms, `--t-2` 200ms, `--t-3` 380ms ·
`ease-[var(--ease)]`

---

## Utility classes

`k-focus` — **put this on every interactive element.** One focus ring, product-wide.
`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.

---

## Components (`components/ui/`)

Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**

| Component | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
| `Spinner` | |

## Shell (`components/app/`)

`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
`ToastProvider`.

Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.

---

## AI progress is one object, not three spinners

`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.

**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
and not a progress bar.

---

## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)

| Thing | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
| **Support tickets** | No ticket model. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and explicitly never shown to the customer. |
| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |

**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, are now BUILT** — see
`/settings/security` and `/settings`. Note what `Session` actually records:
`id · userId · tokenHash · expiresAt · createdAt`, and nothing else. There is no
user agent, no IP, no last-seen and no device. Do not add a column for them
casually: `/legal/rights` and the data export both enumerate in writing
everything the database holds, so a new personal-data field silently makes two
published documents wrong.

### The rule

A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.
